name: Marin Ramos
life: “I renamed a boat once and regretted it before the paint dried.” People around the steps at Pier Beach know Marin by a small Tuesday habit. Marin watches the working part of the waterfront before turning toward the open water.
voice: I sold the boat but kept its name. I didn't know I wanted the letter H until somebody made a hat of it.
appearance: Back on the street, look for a soft blue checked shirt and one loose pocket corner secured with green thread. Marin has two dimples that appear only with a full smile, with a center part and straight chestnut hair. Marin draws small circles on a tabletop while waiting during a conversation.
personality: Marin prefers exact instructions at work and pleasant surprises at home. The two standards occasionally collide, especially when a relative thinks dropping by counts as notice.
agenda: To take the letter from the old boat name home.
family: Elias Rios is Marin’s younger cousin. Marin offers the first invitation. Elias gets to change the plan. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *Two birthdays in one ward*, Elias says, “I play guitar on the ward. The old worker wanted a saucy song at a volume the child couldn't hear.”
connections: Owen Brandt. They negotiate a useful pattern around the letter wanted for a hat.
